Task 1's VALIDATE command is missing its leading `if` keyword: it reads `grep -q '...' && grep -q '...' && grep -q '...' && grep -q '...'; then echo "PASS..."; else echo "FAIL..."; exit 1; fi` with no `if` before the grep chain. This is a bash syntax error ('syntax error near unexpected token `then'') — the script aborts at parse time before any grep ever runs, so the command's exit code reflects a parser failure, never the real presence/absence of the four markers. Fix: prepend `if ` before the first `grep -q`.

Task 1's VALIDATE greps are not byte-exact substrings of Task 1's own ACTION-authored literals. (1) ACTION instructs adding a bullet titled "Always emit `hybrid_code_review: false`" (capital A, mirroring every existing SKILL.md precedent bullet — 'Always emit `docs_sync: true`', 'Always emit `figma_track: false`', 'Always emit `lane_runtime_safe: false`'), but VALIDATE greps case-sensitively (no -i) for the lowercase substring 'always emit `hybrid_code_review: false`', which will not match the capitalized authored text. (2) ACTION instructs writing '...the key is backfilled `hybrid_code_review: false` only when entirely absent' (past-tense 'backfilled'), but VALIDATE greps for the substring 'backfill `hybrid_code_review: false`' (imperative 'backfill' immediately followed by a space then a backtick) — 'backfilled `...' does not contain 'backfill `...' as a substring because 'ed' intervenes before the backtick. Both mismatches mean literal compliance with Task 1's own ACTION prose fails Task 1's own VALIDATE, and would also fail Task 3's downstream gating-structure.mjs marker regexes (`/always emit `hybrid_code_review: false`/i` is case-insensitive so mismatch 1 is masked there, but `/backfill\s*`hybrid_code_review: false`/i` reproduces mismatch 2 identically). Fix: either change the VALIDATE greps to match the precedent's exact casing/verb-form ('Always emit', 'backfill `hybrid_code_review: false`' with the ACTION prose using 'backfill' not 'backfilled'), or change the ACTION prose to author exactly the strings the greps search for.
